scenes.spoken_text: A production plan connects each part to a drawing revision, operation sequence and inspection point. Learn to release work in controlled stages instead of treating a cutting list as a complete manufacturing instruction.
scenes.caption: A production plan connects each part to a drawing revision, operation sequence and inspection point. Learn to release work in controlled stages instead of treating a cutting list as a complete manufacturing instruction.

scenes.spoken_text: Start with an approved drawing revision, stable part codes, material, thickness, grain direction and exposed edges. Distinguish finished size from any process allowance defined by the production method. If a drawing changes, identify affected parts and withdraw obsolete instructions. A part should point to one controlling revision, not leave conflicting dimensions for the operator to resolve.
scenes.caption: Part codes connect drawing, parts list and operation sheet.

scenes.spoken_text: For a teaching cabinet side, identify a datum face, cutting, the system-specific order of edge treatment and holes, then trial assembly. Ask whether the next operation will conceal a measurement surface or block tool access. Some faces may need finishing before assembly. There is no universal sequence; this plan describes outputs and checks, not machine operating procedures.
scenes.caption: Concealed references and access affect the operation order.

scenes.spoken_text: Before repeating the operation across a batch, check the first part against the drawing: code, datum, finished dimensions and prepared features. Record the result, reviewer and release decision. If a mismatch appears, isolate potentially affected parts and identify the last verified stage. Forcing parts together does not replace dimensional checking or correction of the cause.
scenes.caption: First-part approval precedes batch release.

scenes.spoken_text: A teaching batch contains 12 sides. Inspection of the first finds a hole located from the wrong datum. Hold the batch, correct the reference and instructions, and decide the disposition of that part before producing the remaining 11. A tight schedule does not justify repeating the mismatch. Decision: hold repetition, correct the datum, then recheck the first conforming part.
scenes.caption: Decision: hold repetition, correct the datum, then recheck the first conforming part.

scenes.display_title: Prepare a cabinet-side operation sheet with part code, revision, three dependent stages, inspection point and mismatch response.
